# App Workflow

Load TADA File
Flag and Review Sites
Join and Review AUs
Create New AUs (optional)
Join and Review Existing Uses
Assign New Uses
Assign Unique Spatial Criteria (including salt/fresh)
Select Parameters
Assign Parameters to Uses
Create and Review ML Summary Ref

# Tab 1: Load TADA File

Load the TADA water quality data file (output from TADAShiny/Module 1).

This functionality exists in the current draft of TADAShinyJoinToAU but can be simplified. The new version should include only:
- upload/import for water quality TADA file
- button to select file type for upload
- preview of data imported

```{r tada.df}

# load TADA df (mod 1 output)
testdat <- Data_MT_MissoulaCounty
# commented out for if I switch back to tribal data example
# |> dplyr::filter(OrganizationIdentifier == "REDLAKE_WQX")

# preview table
DT::datatable(testdat)

```


# Tab 2: Flag and Review Sites

Runs two functions on the TADA df:
1) TADA_FlagCoordinates
2) TADA_FindNearbySites

Displays a map showing the results of each with the functions:
3)TADA_FlaggedSitesMap
4) TADA_NearbySitesMap

These are two seperate functions. I am not sure whether it is better to display
two seperate maps or figure out a way to modify these functions so they can be
shown as layers that can be toggled on/off within the same map. This might be
most efficient in the Shiny app, but will require some work on the package side
to faciliate.

Displays an editable tables where users can review and edit nearby site groupings and choose to include/exclude monitoring locations based on coordinate flags. The editable tables should
at a minimum include TADA.MonitoringLocationIdentifier, MonitoringLocationIdentifier,
LatitudeMeasure, LongitudeMeasure, OrganizationIdentifier, TADA.SuspectCoordinates.Flag,
and TADA.NearbySitesGroup. I am not sure the best way to accomplish this, but
ideally we could prompt users to review/address any suspect flags from TADA_FlagCoordinates 
before grouping nearby sites with TADA_NearbySites.

The reason for including both the TADA and WQP columns for monitoring location identifier
and the coordinates is that TADA_FindNearbySites may suggest new metadata for some
results if any monitoring locations are grouped.

```{r flag.review.sites}

# run site flagging function
testdat2 <- testdat |>
  TADA_FlagCoordinates() 

# run nearby sites function (temporarily by distance only due to nhd issues)
testdat3 <- testdat2 |>
  TADA_FindNearbySites(catchment = FALSE)

# flagged coordinates map
TADA_FlaggedSitesMap(testdat3)

# nearby sites map
TADA_NearbySitesMap(testdat3)

# subset of data for review table
testdat3_subset <- testdat3 |>
  dplyr::select(TADA.MonitoringLocationIdentifier, 
                MonitoringLocationIdentifier,
                LatitudeMeasure, 
                LongitudeMeasure, 
                OrganizationIdentifier, 
                TADA.SuspectCoordinates.Flag,
                TADA.NearbySiteGroup,
                TADA.NearbySites.Flag) |>
  dplyr::distinct()

# table for review of sites
DT::datatable(testdat3_subset)

```


# Tab 3: Join and Review AUs

User selects organization from a drop down menu. This specifies the organization's
geospatial data that will be used to match WQP monitoring locations with ATTAINS
assessment units.

Users have the option to import their own crosswalk of monitoring locations to
assessment units. This can be a complete crosswalk (contains all monitoring locations)
in the TADA df or a partial crosswalk (contains some of the monitoring locations).
The user's crosswalk is the "au_ref" for TADA_CreateAUMLCrosswalk

Runs: 
1) TADA_CreateAUMLCrosswalk
2) TADA_ViewATTAINS

TADA_CreateAUMLCrosswalk must be run first before its results can be visualized on 
a map using TADA_ViewATTAINS. In the app UI, the TADA_ViewATTAINS map should be 
displayed above an editable table showing the df resulting from TADA_CreateAUMLCrosswalk.
In this table, users can edit the "ATTAINS.AssessmentUnitIdentifier" column.

There should be a way for users to update the TADA_ViewATTAINS map to reflect any
changes they make to the TADA_CreateAUMLCrosswalk table. Automatically updating
is likely no practical (the map function can be a bit slow and users may make 
multiple changes). A simple option like an "Update" button that would need to be 
clickked by the user might work, especially if a message could be displayed when
there are differences between the data in the table and the data underlying the map.

```{r join.aus}

# find AU/ML matches
testdat4 <- TADA_CreateAUMLCrosswalk(testdat3)

# map AUs and MLs
TADA_ViewATTAINS(testdat4)

# subset of AU/ML data for table
testdat4_subset <- testdat4$TADA_with_ATTAINS |>
  dplyr::select(TADA.MonitoringLocationIdentifier,
                TADA.MonitoringLocationName,
                TADA.MonitoringLocationTypeName,
                ATTAINS.AssessmentUnitIdentifier,
                ATTAINS.AssessmentUnitName,
                ATTAINS.WaterType,
                ATTAINS.WaterbodyReportLink) |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry()

# table of AU/ML matches
DT::datatable(testdat4_subset)

# going forward use testdat4's TADA_with_ATTAINS df
testdat5 <- testdat4$TADA_with_ATTAINS

```


# Tab 4: Create New AUs (optional)

This option currently exists for creating new point AUs. This feature was developed
with ATTAINS tribes in mind as many of them use the monitoring location coordinates
as point geometry to create assessment units.

This tab should include a TADA_ViewATTAINS map at the top and below it an editable
data table which contains any monitoring locations that have not been assigned an
assesment unit match in the previous tab. 

Runs:
1) TADA_CreatePointAUs(create_geo = TRUE) on filtered df
2) TADA_ViewATTAINS

Should the TADA_ViewATTAINS map only show the new AUs? Or should it show or have
the option to show all assigned AUs?

The map should be able to be updated if the user edits any fields in the table.

```{r point.aus}

testdat5_noau <- testdat5 |>
  dplyr::filter(is.na(ATTAINS.AssessmentUnitIdentifier)) |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry()
  
testdat5_pointau <- TADA_CreatePointAUs(testdat5_noau, create_geo = TRUE)

# need to wrk on TADA_ViewATTAINS so that it will display output from creating point AUs
TADA_ViewATTAINS(testdat5_pointau$geometry)

DT::datatable(testdat5)

```


# Tab 5: Join and Review Existing Uses

This tab includes a drop down menu with all ATTAINS organizations. It should automatically
be set to match the organization selected in the previous tab.

Users can supply an optional crosswalk of AUs to Uses and/or an optional crosswalk
of Uses to Water Type.

CST uses added optionally here

```{r join.uses}
testdat_uses <- TADA_AssignUsesToAU(testdat5)
```


# Tab 6: Assign New Uses

On this tab, users can assign any new or missing uses to AUs. They will first need
to select either "All" to view all allowable Uses in ATTAINS or can select an 
Organization to view only Uses used by that org (does not have to be their own org).

Once that selection is made, they need to be able to select a UseGroup and view the Uses
within it.

There will be a table showing all AUs along with their Water Types and existing Use
matches. I am not sure the best way to facilitate users adding additional rows to
add new Uses. The table is set up so that there is one row per unique AU/Water Type/Use
combination so adding any new Uses will require appending additional rows.

CST uses added optionally here

```{r new.uses}

# selected org id (or can be "all")
org_id <- "REDLAKE_WQX"


# get allowable domain values for uses
ATTAINS_uses <- rExpertQuery::EQ_DomainValues(domain = "use_name",
                                              api_key = EPATADA:::.setEQKey())

# set up df for use selection
if(org_id != "all") {
  
  ATTAINS_uses <- ATTAINS_uses |>
    dplyr::filter(context == "REDLAKE")
}

ATTAINS_uses <- ATTAINS_uses |>
  dplyr::select(name, context2) |>
  dplyr::distinct() |>
  dplyr::rename(Use = name,
                UseGroup = context2)

#

```


# Tab 7: Assign Unique Spatial Criteria

Users may need to assign additional unique spatial criteria.

There is an EPATADA function, TADA_SaltFreshIndicator that determines whether a
location is saltwater or freshwater. Users decide whether this assignment should
be made based on the ATTAINS Water Type or the WQP monitoring location type (param)

```{r unique.spatial}

# salt/fresh indicator
TADA_SaltFreshIndicator()

```

# Overview and Setup


# Step D: Assign Uses to AUs

After mapping the WQP monitoring locations (MLs) to ATTAINS assessment
units (AUs), we will use the `TADA_AssignUsesToAU` function to assign
specific uses to these assessment units. Additionally, we will
demonstrate how to automatically assign uses to the new assessment unit,
`NEW:EX_MDEQ_WQ_WQX` with the water type "LAKE, FRESHWATER," that was
created in step A, which is not yet present in ATTAINS.

```{r get.MLAURef}
# extract ATTAINS_crosswalk data frame from the list
Final.MT.AUMLRef <- MT.AUMLRef$ATTAINS_crosswalk

# this is the same final output we got above from TADA_CreateAUMLCrosswalk
TADA_TableExport(Final.MT.AUMLRef)
```

Now, we will assign uses to each unique assessment unit (AU) in our
finalized monitoring location to assessment unit crosswalk (e.g.,
`Final.MT.AUMLRef`). The process of assigning uses to AUs follows these
prioritized steps:

1.  User-Supplied Crosswalk (Optional): Utilize a crosswalk provided by
    the user that maps specific uses to assessment units.

2.  Existing Uses from ATTAINS: Import existing uses for assessment
    units as defined by ATTAINS organizations.

```{r assign.use.to.AU, include = F, eval = T}
# use example data, this should be the same as MT.UseAURef
utils::data("Data_MT_AU_UsesRef", package = "EPATADA")
MT.UseAURef <- Data_MT_AU_UsesRef
rm(Data_MT_AU_UsesRef)
```

```{r TADA_AssignUsesToAU, eval = F}
MT.UseAURef <- TADA_AssignUsesToAU(
  MT.AUMLRef$TADA_with_ATTAINS,
  AUMLRef = Final.MT.AUMLRef,
  org_id = "MTDEQ",
  api_key = api_key
)
```

```{r TADA_AssignUsesToAU_table}
TADA_TableExport(MT.UseAURef)
```

#### **Advanced: Assigning Uses to New AUs**

For any new assessment unit (AU), users must determine how to assign the
appropriate uses. The **`TADA_AssignUsesToWaterType`** function is
designed to assist with this process. It imports combinations of water
types and use names associated with the specified organization from
ATTAINS. By doing so, it automatically assigns uses to new assessment
units based on their water type, thereby streamlining the integration of
new AUs into existing frameworks.

For more information on how to customize this function to suit your
needs, enter **`?TADA_AssignUsesToWaterType`** into the R console.

```{r assign.use.to.new.AU.with.waterUseRef_dev, include = F, eval = T}
# use example data, this should be the same as MT.UseAURef_with_WaterUseRef
utils::data("Data_MT_AU_UsesRef_Water", package = "EPATADA")
MT.UseAURef_with_WaterUseRef <- Data_MT_AU_UsesRef_Water
rm(Data_MT_AU_UsesRef_Water)
```

```{r assign.use.to.new.AU.with.waterUseRef_user, eval = FALSE}
MT.UseAURef_with_WaterUseRef <-
  TADA_AssignUsesToAU(
    MT.AUMLRef$TADA_with_ATTAINS,
    waterUseRef = TADA_AssignUsesToWaterType(org_id = "MTDEQ"),
    AUMLRef = Final.MT.AUMLRef,
    org_id = "MTDEQ",
    api_key = api_key
  )
```

```{r watertypetable}
TADA_TableExport(MT.UseAURef_with_WaterUseRef)
```

Users also have the option to manually assign use names to new AUs if
they prefer not to use the TADA_AssignUsesToWaterType function. This
approach allows for greater flexibility and customization when
integrating new AUs into existing frameworks.

```{r assign.use.to.new.AU.manual}
MT.UseAURef_manual <- MT.UseAURef |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    data.frame(
      ATTAINS.UseName = c("Aquatic Life", "Drinking Water"),
      ATTAINS.AssessmentUnitIdentifier = c("NEW:EX_MDEQ_WQ_WQX", "NEW:EX_MDEQ_WQ_WQX")
    ),
    by = ("ATTAINS.AssessmentUnitIdentifier")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ATTAINS.UseName = dplyr::coalesce(ATTAINS.UseName.x, ATTAINS.UseName.y)) |>
  dplyr::select(-ATTAINS.UseName.x, -ATTAINS.UseName.y)

TADA_TableExport(MT.UseAURef_manual)
```

# Summary

In conclusion, this example TADA Module 2 workflow significantly
enhances the ability to maintain up-to-date information on WQP
Monitoring Locations and the uses being assessed at various ATTAINS
Assessment Units. By systematically guiding users through the creation
of crosswalks, map reviews, data submission, and use assignments, this
workflow supports efficient data management and improves
reproducibility.
